French, Spanish & Mandarin
Bonjour, Hola and Nǐ hǎo!
From Pre-Reception onwards, children embark on a language-learning journey that begins with French and grows to include Spanish and Mandarin as they progress through the school. Through stories, songs, games and conversation, languages are brought to life in a fun and immersive environment that sparks curiosity, builds confidence and opens doors to new cultures, traditions and opportunities.
Inspiring a Love of Languages
Our specialist French and Spanish teacher, Mrs Stubberfield, brings warmth, energy and a genuine passion for languages to every lesson in our bright and colourful Languages Room. Through songs, stories, games and cultural experiences, she inspires children to embrace new sounds, celebrate having a go and discover the joy of communicating in another language. Through vocabulary, phonics and grammar, children grow in confidence, make connections between languages and develop an appreciation of the wider world.
I believe languages should be an adventure. My ambition is for every child to leave Chinthurst eager to explore new cultures, willing to take risks and excited to communicate in another language
Sam Stubberfield, Head of Languages
Our youngest learners in Pre-Reception enjoy a weekly French lesson with Mrs Stubberfield, where they discover new words and sounds through stories, music, games and imaginative play. These engaging sessions spark curiosity, build confidence and encourage children to explore the wider world.
Children in Reception build on these foundations in their weekly French lessons. Activities are themed around familiar and exciting topics, such as French food and pirates, helping children to extend their vocabulary and begin using simple words and phrases with increasing confidence.
In Years 1 and 2, children learn both French and Spanish in alternate half terms. Lessons continue to be themed around engaging topics, with a focus on listening and speaking, alongside the gradual introduction of writing skills.
In Years 3 and 4, children have weekly French and Spanish lessons, developing their cultural awareness alongside vocabulary, pronunciation and conversational skills in both languages. Mandarin Club is also available during lunchtime, offering a fun introduction to an additional language and culture. Through games, songs, storytelling, crafts and interactive activities, children learn simple greetings, numbers and everyday words while discovering Chinese festivals, traditions and customs. The club sparks curiosity, builds confidence and provides a gentle introduction to Mandarin before formal lessons begin in Year 5.
Spanish Club is available to all children from Year 3 upwards as part of our after-school clubs programme.
In Years 5 and 6, children study both Mandarin and French as part of their weekly timetable. Through expert teaching, they develop the confidence to introduce themselves, talk about their family, hobbies, dates and festivals, ask and answer simple questions, and recognise and write a selection of Chinese characters. They develop accurate pronunciation through Pinyin, learn to distinguish the four tones and gain a deeper appreciation of Chinese culture through activities such as calligraphy, traditional celebrations and the exploration of customs and traditions.
Language learning culminates in a Year 6 residential trip to France, where children experience French language and culture first-hand. It is a much-anticipated experience and a treasured highlight of many children's time at Chinthurst.
Spanish Club is available to all children from Year 3 upwards as part of our after-school clubs programme.
Specialist teaching and resourcing in areas such as art, drama, music, physical education (PE), French, Spanish and Mandarin encourage pupils' individual interests and self-motivation

Drama
After all, the world's a stage and, at Chinthurst, every child is given the confidence to take their place on it.
Drama is at the heart of life at Chinthurst. From Pre-Reception to Year 6, every child enjoys drama lessons that build confidence, creativity and communication skills while having fun.
In the Upper School, lessons are led by our specialist Drama teacher, Mrs Stricker-Timmermans (known to the children as Mrs S-T), whose passion and expertise inspire children to develop their performance skills, confidence and creativity. Through improvisation, storytelling, characterisation, movement and performance, children learn to express themselves, work collaboratively and develop the confidence to step outside their comfort zone. Every term brings new opportunities to explore different aspects of drama in a supportive and engaging environment.
From September 2026, Drama will have a new home in our purpose-built Creative Arts Building, providing an inspiring space where children can rehearse, perform and develop their creativity as part of our thriving performing arts programme.
Opportunities to Shine
Performance is a celebrated part of the Chinthurst experience. From Nativity plays in Nursery to Year 2, to productions in Years 3, 4, 5 and 6, every child has the opportunity to shine. In Year 5, children devise and create their own production, developing creative and performance skills that provide an excellent foundation for senior school and beyond. By the time they reach Year 6, children take part in a major production that showcases the confidence, resilience and teamwork they have developed throughout their journey.
Performance opportunities are woven throughout school life. Each week, a different class leads a whole-school assembly at our local church, sharing their learning with fellow children, staff and parents. These regular opportunities to speak and perform in front of an audience help children develop confidence, communication skills and self-belief from an early age.
Excellence in Performance
Children from Year 1 to Year 6 can take individual LAMDA lessons as part of our peripatetic programme, developing skills in acting, public speaking and communication. As a registered LAMDA examination centre, Chinthurst has built an outstanding reputation for excellence, with more than a third of our children choosing to participate in the programme. Our results are consistently exceptional, with 93% of children achieving Distinction grades last year and the remaining children awarded Merits. These achievements reflect the high-quality teaching, dedication and enthusiasm that underpin our drama provision.
Beyond examinations, LAMDA helps children develop confidence, self-expression and resilience – skills that support them both in school and throughout their lives. The strength of Drama at Chinthurst is reflected in the many drama scholarships our children are awarded as they move on to senior school each year.
Confidence for Life
Drama at Chinthurst is about much more than performing on stage. Through regular opportunities to speak, present and perform, children develop the confidence, resilience and communication skills that will serve them throughout their lives. They learn to express their ideas clearly, speak in front of an audience, collaborate with others and think creatively, while developing empathy, perseverance and self-belief.
The impact can be seen across the school community. Our children are comfortable speaking with visitors, making eye contact and sharing their thoughts with confidence and respect. They learn how to present themselves positively in interviews and new situations, stand up for what is right and embrace challenges with determination. Senior schools frequently comment on the maturity, confidence and communication skills of Chinthurst children - qualities that become part of the Chinthurst spirit and help them thrive long after they leave us.

Music
Step into Chinthurst and, within minutes, you'll hear music - it's truly the heartbeat of our school.
Inspiring a Love of Music
Music plays a central role in both everyday life and special occasions, and our children embrace it with enthusiasm and joy. Whether singing together in assembly, rehearsing with one of our choirs, performing in the orchestra or learning a new instrument, they are immersed in a vibrant musical culture that brings our community together and provides opportunities for everyone to shine.
Led by our Head of Music, Laura Oldfield, we believe that music is for everyone. It is a powerful way for children to express themselves, build confidence and creativity, and experience the satisfaction of working towards a shared goal. Along the way, they develop many of the qualities we value at Chinthurst, including resilience, collaboration, discipline and critical thinking.
Music in the Classroom
All children benefit from specialist music teaching throughout their time at the school. Through singing, performing, composing and listening, they develop musical skills while exploring a wide range of cultures, genres and historical periods. Singing lies at the heart of our curriculum and is woven into school life through weekly singing practices, assemblies, performances and choir rehearsals.
Our curriculum includes a variety of whole-class instrumental experiences, allowing children to discover different instruments and musical styles. From recorder in Year 2 and violin in Year 3 to ukulele and keyboard in Year 4 and African djembe drumming in Year 5, children enjoy practical, hands-on learning that builds musical confidence and understanding. They also explore music technology and composition, developing their creativity through both traditional and modern approaches to music-making.
Beyond the Classroom
Music thrives beyond the classroom through our extensive peripatetic music programme. More than 165 individual music lessons take place each week with our specialist visiting music teachers, covering a wide range of instruments including piano, violin, cello, flute, guitar, drums, trumpet, saxophone, voice and musical theatre.
Children can also take part in our award-winning choirs, orchestra and other ensembles. These groups provide opportunities to perform together, develop teamwork and build confidence, while sharing a love of music with friends across the school.
Performance Opportunities
Performing is an important part of musical life at Chinthurst. Throughout the year, children have many opportunities to take to the stage in concerts, assemblies, productions, festivals and community events. They share their music with audiences in a range of settings, from local care homes and the Ashley Centre in Epsom to prestigious venues such as Battersea Arts Centre, while also achieving success at local music festivals.
These experiences help children develop confidence, stage presence and the excitement of performing for others.
A Lifelong Love of Music
Above all, music at Chinthurst is inclusive, ambitious and full of enjoyment. Whether a child is taking their first musical steps or developing an exceptional talent, we provide the encouragement, opportunities and inspiration for every child to flourish, express themselves creatively and develop a lasting appreciation of music.

The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) Reports
Chinthurst is delighted to announce that it has successfully met all the required standards following its inspection in February 2026.
The ISI inspects schools according to a standard framework for inspection which it has laid down for the purposes of ensuring that standards are maintained and that the school complies with relevant legal requirements. This framework has been agreed with the Department for Education and they have recognised the ISI as the body responsible for the regular inspection of schools in England which are affiliated to the ISC.
All pupils are encouraged to be ambitious and participate in the wide-ranging opportunities available to them with resilience, confidence and enthusiasm
Inspectors also identified a Significant Strength at the school. Within the ISI framework, this recognition is awarded only in a small minority of inspections, highlighting an aspect of a school’s provision that has an exceptional and meaningful impact on pupils.
The inspection team recognised the outstanding culture of kindness, respect and inclusion that defines daily life at Chinthurst. Pupils demonstrated a strong understanding that people may be different and that everyone should feel valued and included.
Read our latest ISI Inspection 2026 report
You can also access our previous reports from 2023 and 2018, or visit the Independent Schools Inspectorate website for earlier editions.

Computing
Please don’t take it personally if your child is more excited to tell you about coding a robot, turning a banana into a piano or designing a 3D creation than what they had for lunch.
Technology Across the Curriculum
Embedded throughout the curriculum from age two and taught as a stand-alone subject, it underpins learning across every area of school life. From problem-solving in maths and science to creative projects in art and design, children learn to think critically, logically and imaginatively with technology at their fingertips. Whether discovering the depths of the ocean in science, travelling to far-flung corners of the globe in geography or stepping back in time to explore ancient civilisations in history through Virtual Reality headsets, technology brings learning vividly to life. Alongside coding and digital literacy, children begin to understand how emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, are shaping the world around them.
At Chinthurst, computing empowers children to become creators rather than consumers of technology. Through coding, design and digital exploration, they develop the confidence, creativity and critical thinking skills needed for an ever-changing world.
Kate Gilmore, Computing Lead
Building Confidence with Technology in the Lower School
From Reception, children begin exploring technology in a variety of engaging ways. Indi Cars introduce coding through hands-on challenges that progress from Reception to Year 2, while Busy Things supports learning across the curriculum. Purple Mash further develops coding and creativity through links with Maths, English and creative projects. By Years 1 and 2, children confidently use iPads to research, animate and code using Scratch Junior, strengthening their creativity, problem-solving and independence. Children also develop early coding vocabulary through both digital and real-life activities, learning key concepts such as algorithms and debugging.
In weekly Computing lessons in Reception, children use iPads and desktop computers to build digital literacy skills, practising keyboard and mouse control alongside creative apps. These lessons support fine motor development and confidence with age-appropriate software, culminating in the final half term when children create their own digital music. Online safety is a key focus throughout, as children learn how to stay safe when using technology.
In Years 1 and 2, children are taught by a specialist teacher in our dedicated IT suite, building on their early experience of touchscreen and keyboard-based technology. Year 1 pupils develop their skills through activities such as Indi Cars, LEGO Builders, animated storybooks, Scratch Junior and designing their own maze games. In Year 2, learning progresses to using Microsoft Word, Scratch, 2Code on Purple Mash and computer art, further enhancing their technical skills and creativity.
Designing, Programming and Innovating in the Upper School
In the Upper School, computing lessons take coding and creativity to the next level. Years 3 and 4 enjoy one dedicated Computing lesson each week, increasing to two lessons per week in Years 5 and 6. Using Sphero Bolt+ robots, children move beyond the basics to programme complex movements, integrate sensors and tackle challenges like real engineers. They also develop digital storytelling through stop-motion animation and explore 3D design with TinkerCAD and our 3D printers, producing everything from marble mazes to practical pen pots.
iPads are used across all year groups, enriching learning in every subject. By Years 5 and 6, children advance to Surface Go laptops, building the digital skills they need for senior school and beyond. They also innovate with Makey Makey kits, transforming bananas into pianos or playdough into keyboards, proving that computing at Chinthurst is as much about imagination as it is about code.
Teachers are knowledgeable and skilled in the areas that they teach.

Science
A passion for Science begins with memorable experiences – doing it, smelling it, touching it, squishing it and asking questions about the world around us.
Learning by Doing
These are the moments that become core memories, spark curiosity and help every child to leave Chinthurst with a genuine love of Science and a desire to keep discovering more.
Science at Chinthurst is practical, hands-on and often gloriously messy. Our Science curriculum encourages children to think critically, investigate independently and make connections between what they learn in the classroom and the world around them. Every lesson includes investigation and experimentation, with children taking the lead as scientists themselves rather than simply watching their teacher demonstrate. Whether building robotic lighthouses in Year 3, exploring peristalsis with tights in Year 4, or dissecting hearts in Year 6, children learn by doing.
Science should be something children remember with a smile. If they can smell it, touch it, squish it and investigate it for themselves, they won't just understand Science – they'll love it.
Ruth Read, Science Lead
Discovering Science Through Exploration
Scientific thinking begins long before formal investigations. From Nursery onwards, children are encouraged to question, explore and make sense of the world around them through first-hand experiences.
In the Lower School, our weekly Discovery Afternoons provide rich opportunities for children to develop scientific knowledge and enquiry skills through outdoor learning, gardening, environmental projects, Forest School and STEAM challenges. Children learn to observe closely, ask questions, make predictions and test their ideas while investigating the natural world around them.
These meaningful, hands-on experiences help children develop curiosity, resilience and problem-solving skills, providing strong foundations for the increasingly sophisticated scientific enquiry they encounter as they move through the school.
We want our children to experience science rather than simply learn about it. Discovery Afternoons give them the opportunity to explore, investigate and make meaningful connections with the world around them.
Toni Burton, Head of Lower School
Preparing for the Next Stage
All children in Years 3 to 6 enjoy a double Science lesson each week in our well-equipped Science Lab. By Year 6, children confidently plan, conduct and analyse their own investigations, drawing conclusions from evidence and communicating their findings with confidence. They can even dissect a heart, not only to understand its structure and function, but also to develop the practical and analytical skills needed to investigate complex scientific questions.
They leave Chinthurst familiar with using a wide range of scientific equipment, preparing slides and specimens, working with microscopes and recording their observations accurately, giving them the confidence and skills to make a smooth transition to senior school Science.
Bringing Science to Life
Science is embraced across the whole school and celebrated well beyond weekly lessons. British Science Week is always a highlight, with children taking part in whole-school Science Curriculum Days packed with fun, hands-on challenges and memorable experiences.
Activities have included immersive journeys through the Science Dome, transporting children to the wonders of space exploration without ever leaving the school grounds, alongside visits from inspiring speakers and interactive science demonstrations led by teachers from our senior school, Reigate Grammar School. Educational visits further enrich learning throughout the year, with trips to the Observatory Science Centre in Herstmonceux, Haslemere Museum to explore fossils and rocks, Wisley Gardens, Juniper Hall and the Living Rainforest.
These experiences bring learning to life, deepen understanding and create lasting memories that inspire children to keep questioning, discovering and developing a lifelong love of Science.
Pupils are taught an appropriate range of other subjects such as science, humanities, and information and communication technology (ICT) which broaden pupils' knowledge, skills and understanding.

Clubs
A new passion can begin with simply having the chance to try something new.
We’re proud to offer an exciting and varied clubs programme, with over 50 activities available to suit every interest and personality. From sporty adventurers to creative minds, there truly is something for everyone! Clubs run before school, at lunchtime and after school, giving children plenty of opportunities to explore new hobbies, develop skills and have fun with friends.
Some clubs are offered free of charge, while others are led by trusted external providers and are payable. Our programme is open to all children from Nursery to Year 6, with activities carefully tailored to suit each age group. The selection for each age range changes every term, keeping things fresh and exciting, but typically includes:
Our clubs programme is all about helping children discover new passions, build confidence and, most importantly, have fun!
Pupils' learning is enriched through the programme of trips, clubs and activities which extends pupils' interests and allows them to develop new skills. Opportunities include languages, chess, a wide range of sports, creative arts, mindfulness and dancing, as well as musical ensembles. These experiences help pupils to develop their strategic thinking, performance skills and physical health successfully.

Food Glorious Food
Lunchtime is a highlight of the day for many children at Chinthurst - and it’s easy to see why!
Delicious, Nutritious Lunchtimes at Chinthurst
Every day, our children enjoy a delicious selection of nutritious, home-cooked meals lovingly prepared by our wonderful catering team.
Our catering is provided by external catering company, Lodestone House, whose mission is to bring fresh, seasonal ingredients to the dishes our children eat in school. This commitment to quality and variety inspires the fantastic range of lunchtime options available each day.
Our weekly menus run on a three-week rotation and are refreshed every term, ensuring there is always something new and exciting to enjoy. Alongside the daily hot meal choices, children can also choose from jacket potatoes, pasta dishes, an extensive salad bar, soup and fresh fruit, all available every day.
Introducing our Catering Team
Leading our catering team are our brilliant Catering Manager, Rute, and our Head Chef, Vicky. As well as overseeing food supplies and managing costs, Rute is also a talented chef and baker, responsible for many of the delicious homemade cakes enjoyed by both children and visitors alike. Guests at Chinthurst events such as our Time to Talk Café, Sports Day and Grandparents’ Morning are always spoilt for choice by the tempting array of freshly baked treats on offer. Vicky is responsible for cooking the children’s favourite meals and is well known to them all, helping to ensure they eat a well-balanced meal each day.
Caring for Every Child
At Chinthurst, the wellbeing of every child is our priority, and we take allergies and dietary requirements extremely seriously. We aim to be a nut and sesame seed free school and work closely with families to support children with individual allergies, intolerances and special dietary needs. Our catering team carefully prepares meals to ensure that every child can enjoy safe, nutritious and delicious food each day.

Our Houses
A vibrant and active House System
At Chinthurst, our four Houses are a key part of school life, bringing children together and helping to create a strong sense of community. Dragon in purple, Griffin in yellow, Pegasus in blue and Phoenix in red, each have their own proud identity, with children wearing their House colours and waving their flags with pride at events throughout the year. Through regular House assemblies, events and competitions, children feel part of something bigger, building friendships across year groups along the way.
The House System offers a wide range of opportunities, from charity fundraising and leadership roles to friendly competition. Highlights include:
Each House is led by a Head of House and supported by our Year 6 House Captains, who take pride in developing and demonstrating their leadership skills. Children are encouraged to take part, support one another and enjoy everything their House has to offer.
Meet the Heads of Houses
Leaders offer a range of opportunities to encourage pupils' service to the school community through various leadership roles and charitable initiatives.

Sustainability
Imagine a school where children don't just learn about the environment - they help protect it.
One day they might be planting flowers for pollinators, the next leading a recycling campaign, exploring woodland habitats or taking part in a national environmental initiative. Along the way, they discover that even the smallest actions can make a meaningful difference.
Through outdoor learning, our award-winning Eco-Schools programme and environmental themes woven throughout the curriculum, children develop a lifelong respect for nature, a sense of responsibility for the world around them and the confidence to become thoughtful global citizens.
Eco-Schools Green Flag Award with Distinction
We are proud to hold the Eco-Schools Green Flag Award with Distinction, recognising our whole-school commitment to sustainability and environmental education.
During the assessment, Eco-Schools praised the impact of environmental learning at Chinthurst School. Following a whole-school survey, 75% of children said they are now committed to reducing their use of plastics, demonstrating the positive difference our work is making.
Our enthusiastic Eco Committee leads many of our environmental initiatives, giving children the opportunity to share ideas, organise projects and encourage sustainable habits across the school.
Your teaching is inspiring real, lasting behaviour change
Susta​​​​​inability in Action
Caring for the environment is part of everyday life at Chinthurst. Children recycle, take part in local litter picks, reduce waste, save energy and are encouraged to use reusable water bottles and lunch containers.
Our grounds provide rich opportunities to connect with nature through outdoor learning and biodiversity projects. Children help create habitats for wildlife, plant flowers and trees for pollinators and, from September 2026, will enjoy a new Lower School garden. Nursery (Acorns), Pre-Reception and Reception children also enjoy regular Woodland Learning afternoons in the local area, encouraging curiosity, resilience and an appreciation of the natural world from an early age.
Across the curriculum, sustainability is explored through science, geography and PSHE, where children investigate climate change, biodiversity, conservation and responsible living. They also learn about protecting oceans and rivers while discovering how caring for nature supports both the planet and our own wellbeing.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Children regularly take part in national environmental campaigns, including The Big Plastic Count, support organisations such as the WWF and Surrey Wildlife Trust, and celebrate environmental achievements in assemblies and newsletters. They also have the opportunity to complete Bikeability in Years 4 and 6, promoting safe, active and sustainable travel.
By giving children meaningful opportunities to care for the environment today, we are helping them grow into compassionate, responsible young people who are ready to make a positive difference tomorrow.

Swim School
Every child has the chance to make a splash and grow in confidence in the water.
We're proud to have our own indoor heated swimming pool at Chinthurst. All children in Reception to Year 2 enjoy weekly swimming lessons throughout the year, while children in Years 3 to 6 take part in swimming during two half terms as part of their PE programme.
Our pool is also home to JG Swimming, an independent swim school based on site. Their classes cater for a wide range of ages and abilities, complementing the school’s swimming lessons and helping children build confidence in the water.
Sessions run daily after school, with additional crash courses available during the holidays. For full details and to book, please visit www.jgswimming.co.uk.

Trips, Visits & Residentials
Some of the most powerful learning happens when children step beyond the familiar and experience something new.
Educational Visits, Residentials and Visiting Speakers
Imagine climbing aboard a real fire engine in Reception, learning woodland survival skills on your first residential in Year 4, kayaking with friends in Year 5 and staying in a French château in Year 6. At Chinthurst, learning extends far beyond the classroom. Educational visits, residential adventures, visiting speakers and hands-on workshops spark curiosity, nurture confidence and create memories that last a lifetime. From Nursery to Year 6, every opportunity is carefully chosen to enrich the curriculum and help children develop independence, resilience and teamwork.
Bringing Learning to Life
Our youngest children delight in memorable experiences that make learning meaningful. Nursery and Reception children enjoy Little City role-play workshops, transforming the Lower School Hall into a bustling miniature town complete with construction sites, emergency services, a supermarket, hair salon and doctor's surgery. Reception also visit local places such as Bocketts Farm and welcome special visitors to school, including firefighters who arrive in a real fire engine and demonstrate how they help our community. Taking turns to direct the fire hose across the playing field is always a particular highlight!
As they move through the Lower School, children enjoy a range of inspiring trips and workshops linked to their learning. Highlights include visits to Gatton Park, Leeds Castle, Wisley Gardens and Drusillas Park, alongside immersive theatre experiences that bring topics such as the Great Fire of London vividly to life.
From Year 3 onwards, learning becomes even more adventurous. Highlights include exploring geology and natural history at Haslemere Museum, taking part in environmental studies at Juniper Hall and stepping back in time through Viking, Saxon and Roman workshops held at school.
Year 4 marks children's first overnight residential, where they begin to discover what they can achieve beyond their comfort zone. Experiences have included mastering archery and orienteering, building woodland survival skills, tackling team challenges and gathering around the campfire to toast marshmallows, share stories and sing songs beneath the stars. Visits such as The Living Rainforest and engaging Roman workshops further enrich their studies.
In Year 5, children enjoy a two-night outdoor adventure residential packed with opportunities to challenge themselves, support one another and embrace new experiences. Activities may include kayaking, canoeing, paddleboarding, fencing, crate stacking and problem-solving challenges, alongside visits and workshops that bring science vividly to life.
Year 6 children create some of their most treasured Chinthurst memories during a four-night residential in France, staying in a beautiful château, developing their language skills, experiencing a different culture and building confidence through international travel. Among the many opportunities on offer, children also take part in Junior Citizen Day, learning valuable life skills and how to stay safe in a variety of real-world situations.
Learning from Experts
Throughout the year, children benefit from an inspiring programme of visiting speakers, authors, performers, historians and scientists who spark new interests and broaden horizons. Travelling theatre companies and specialist visitors transport children back in time, bringing topics such as the Great Fire of London, the Romans, Vikings and Saxons vividly to life. Whether dressing up as Roman soldiers, handling replica artefacts, meeting Viking warriors or taking part in immersive performances, children are encouraged to ask questions, think creatively and fully immerse themselves in their learning.
My favourite memory of Chinthurst is one of the most amazing trips I have ever experienced: the French Trip! It was so much fun and really exciting. I made so many awesome memories that I know I will never forget.
Chinthurst Class of 2025 Alumna and RGS Student

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care & Holiday Camps
School life should work for the whole family, from the first drop-off of the day to the final pick-up.
Term Time
During term time, children from Nursery to Year 6 are warmly welcomed into our wraparound care provision.
After school, children can enjoy an extensive range of exciting extra-curricular clubs run by teaching staff and external club providers which are both free and paid for clubs.
We also offer Lower School Sibling Care, and Aftercare available to all children from Nursery to Year 6. See more information below.
Learn more about our Clubs
We also offer a paid aftercare service for children from Nursery to Year 6, where they can enjoy a wide range of activities after school, as well as a hot tea. Parents are welcome to collect their children at any time up until 6.00pm (or 5.00pm on Fridays). Sessions are booked online in advance.
Our sessions strike the perfect balance between fun and relaxation. Alongside games and group activities, there are calm moments for reading stories or enjoying some quiet downtime when needed, ensuring every child feels happy, settled and supported. Upper School children are given the opportunity to complete their homework, spellings or reading during the session, helping to ease the pressure for busy working parents.
There are wraparound care spaces available for everyone and a booking system, via a bespoke app, that gives parents the flexibility to confirm sessions well in advance or right up to the evening before.
Holiday Clubs
During the school holidays, Chinthurst is proud to host holiday camps run by Camp Beaumont, a highly respected and long-established UK provider of holiday childcare. With over 40 years’ experience, Camp Beaumont has an excellent reputation for delivering exciting, high-quality activity days for children aged 3 years and above.
Learn more about Camp Beaumont
Our holiday camps create magical, inspiring and confidence-building experiences tailored to each age group. Children can look forward to over 50 exhilarating indoor and outdoor activities including Superhero Academy, Soft Play Ninjas, Clay Workshop, Aqua Olympics, Mini Archery and Rockstar Challenge. Our camps give children the chance to make new friends, have fun away from screens and enjoy a friendly, welcoming environment. With flexible booking options, childcare vouchers and tax-free childcare accepted, Camp Beaumont is a convenient and affordable choice for busy families

pageCache.text:
Moving to Senior School
Choosing a senior school is a significant milestone for any family.
Every child is different, with their own talents, ambitions and personality, and our role is to help them move on to a school where they will feel happy, confident and ready to flourish.
Finding the Right Fit for Every Child
At Chinthurst, senior school preparation is about much more than passing exams. It’s about getting to know each child exceptionally well, celebrating their strengths and guiding families towards the setting that feels right for them. Whether children continue their journey within the Reigate Grammar School family or explore other independent and state schools, we are there to support and advise every step of the way.
A Personalised Journey
Conversations about senior schools begin in Year 3, giving families plenty of time to explore the options available and consider what matters most for their child. Through information events, individual meetings and ongoing discussions, our Future Schools Team works closely with families to help them navigate the process with confidence.
As children progress through the Upper School, we develop a detailed understanding of their academic profile, interests, character and aspirations. This enables us to provide thoughtful advice and identify the schools where they are most likely to be happy, successful and able to make the most of the opportunities on offer.
Years 3 and 4
During Years 3 and 4, families are introduced to the senior school journey and the different routes available. Children continue to strengthen their academic foundations, develop reasoning skills and grow in independence, while parents have opportunities to discuss future aspirations and possible destinations.
Year 5
By Year 5, the process becomes more focused. Every child receives an early offer to either Reigate Grammar School or RGS Surrey Hills, giving families reassurance and clarity as they consider their next steps.
For those exploring other senior schools, our dedicated 11+ Lead provides tailored guidance and support with entrance assessments, interviews and scholarship applications.
Year 6
Children applying to schools beyond the RGS family continue to benefit from targeted preparation and interview practice throughout Year 6. At the same time, all children embark on our bespoke Reigate Ready programme, which develops independence, resilience and the confidence needed for a smooth transition to senior school.
Two Routes, One Destination
The RGS Family Route
As part of the Reigate Grammar School family, Chinthurst children can receive an early offer of a place at either Reigate Grammar School or RGS Surrey Hills without sitting an entrance examination.
This approach allows children to enjoy a rich and varied final year at Chinthurst, free from unnecessary exam pressure, while benefiting from strong pastoral links and a shared educational ethos.
The 11+ Route
For families considering schools beyond the RGS family, Chinthurst offers a highly successful and personalised 11+ programme.
Led by our dedicated 11+ specialist, children receive expert preparation for assessments, interviews and scholarship applications, while continuing to enjoy the broad curriculum, leadership opportunities, productions, residentials and extracurricular activities that make life at Chinthurst so memorable.
Outstanding Outcomes
Chinthurst has an exceptional record of helping children secure places at the senior school where they will thrive.
For our 2025–26 Year 6 cohort:
The excellent teaching and well-rounded lives of the Chinthurst pupils ably prepares them for success and achievement in their secondary education
Shaun Fenton, Headmaster, Reigate Grammar School
100% secured a senior school place

Year 3–6 (Upper School)
Upper School is where growing confidence opens the door to new challenges, greater independence and exciting possibilities.
Learning Without Limits
One minute children might be discussing whether peace is more important than money, the next they could be designing a computer game, rehearsing for a production, competing in a sports fixture, mentoring a younger child or preparing to sell products they have created for charity. These are years filled with challenge, discovery and opportunity, where children are encouraged to think deeply, embrace new experiences and grow in confidence as learners and as individuals.
Encompassing Years 3 to 6 and based in Morris House, Upper School at Chinthurst is a place where childhood curiosity continues to flourish alongside growing independence, responsibility and academic ambition. Building on the strong foundations established in Lower School, children embark on an exciting and enriching journey that prepares them for senior school and beyond.
The curriculum is broad, balanced and inclusive
Academic Excellence, Powered by Heart
At Chinthurst, we believe children learn best when they are engaged, challenged and having fun. Lessons are lively, practical and carefully planned to encourage collaboration, creativity and independent thinking. Small classes and strong relationships with staff ensure every child is known as an individual and receives the support and stretch they need to flourish. Whether experimenting in the science laboratory, debating philosophical questions, bringing ideas to life through coding and 3D design, or exploring the outdoors, children are encouraged to immerse themselves in their learning, take risks, ask questions and discover new interests and talents. Specialist teaching, educational visits, residentials and visiting experts further enrich the curriculum and help bring learning to life.
Underpinning everything we do is our bespoke Wellbeing at Heart programme, which supports children to develop resilience, confidence and a strong sense of self. Find out more...
Trips & Residentials
A Broad and Enriching Curriculum
English, mathematics, science, computing and the humanities remain at the heart of the curriculum, while an increasing number of subjects are taught by specialists who bring expertise, passion and fresh perspectives to children's learning.
Upper School children benefit from specialist teaching in art and design technology, drama, French, Spanish, Mandarin, music, computing, PE and games. These subjects enrich the curriculum, encourage creativity and collaboration, and help children develop confidence, resilience and self-motivation.
Growing Through the Upper School Years
Year 3 marks an exciting step into our Upper School and Key Stage 2. Alongside greater independence and higher expectations, children continue to enjoy a curriculum filled with creativity, exploration and fun. They begin representing the school in sports fixtures, sing in one of our Upper School choirs and take a more active role within the House system, competing for honours in events such as the Performing Arts Cup. Trips, visiting workshops and practical learning experiences help bring subjects to life and inspire curiosity.
As confidence grows, Year 4 children are encouraged to take increasing ownership of their learning and embrace new challenges. They enjoy their first overnight residential adventure, curriculum-enhancing trips such as the Living Rainforest and an increasing range of opportunities to contribute to school life. Families also begin to explore senior school pathways through information events and learn more about the Early Offer process to our senior schools, helping them to plan confidently for the future.
Year 5 is a year of growing maturity and responsibility. Children enjoy an exciting two-night residential packed with outdoor challenges, teamwork and problem-solving activities, alongside visits such as the Science Observatory. They become trained Peer Mediators, supporting younger children and promoting kindness and friendship across the school. By Year 5, children have either received an Early Offer to Reigate Grammar School or RGS Surrey Hills, or are following our tailored 11+ programme led by Mr Beadle, giving them clarity and confidence as they prepare for senior school.
By Year 6, children are confident, independent learners and positive role models for the rest of the school. Every child undertakes a position of responsibility during the year, whether as Head Boy or Head Girl, House Captain, Music Prefect or in another leadership role. They also complete training as Peer Mentors, developing their understanding of mental health, active listening and how to support others with empathy and care.
Year 6 children become young entrepreneurs through their business enterprise project, designing, producing and marketing their own products before selling them to raise money for charity. Their final year at Chinthurst is packed with memorable experiences, including the Year 6 Production, final self-portrait projects in art, a special Treat Day organised by Year 6 Class Reps, an end-of-year sleepover and their final Chinthurst adventure - a residential visit to Normandy, where they immerse themselves in French language and culture while developing independence, resilience and lasting memories with friends.
Children leave Chinthurst academically prepared, emotionally secure and ready to embrace senior school with confidence, kindness and enthusiasm.
Specialist teaching and resourcing in areas such as art, drama, music, physical education (PE), French, Spanish and Mandarin encourage pupils' individual interests and self-motivation

Don’t just take our word for it. Hear what others have to say.
Muddy Stilettos
Muddy Stilettos, the award-winning lifestyle site loved by parents across Surrey and beyond, visited Chinthurst to discover what makes our school so special - and we were delighted with their glowing review.
“Chinthurst nursery and prep school has a strong family-friendly vibe and a big emphasis on community – add to this outstanding academics and the outcome is happy children with great results!”
The school’s big calling card is its pastoral care and wellbeing. It’s intrinsic within the school’s ethos and structure – and it shows.
“The school takes a progressive and forward-looking approach to sport, particularly when it comes to gender equality…Their innovative approach to sport caught the attention of the judges of the Independent School of the Year awards, and in 2022 the school was awarded 2022 Independent School of the Year for Sporting Achievement… Safe to say, Chinthurst punches well above its weight when it comes to sports.”
“As a fully integrated part of Chinthurst School, the joined-up Nursery curriculum ensures the children are well prepared for the step up to Reception when the time comes.”
Read the full Muddy Stilettos review
Surrey's "Miss Honey"
Our Head, Cathy Trundle, is in the spotlight in lifestyle website Muddy Stilettos’ Heads Up! series. This is what Muddy Stilettos had to say when introducing Cathy Trundle’s feature:
“Step aside Miss Trunchbull - we've found the Miss Honey of Surrey schools.”
“Genuinely, she's one of the loveliest people you will ever meet. Kind, caring and passionate about education with a determination to make school fun and interesting for her charges, and to get the very best out of them. Which she does!”
